requests: Explain the best way to drywall the 9-inch concrete-block ledge, given the uneven block and top-plate surface and the lack of framing at the back.
Say whether proper flat and level framing needs to be built out.
Say whether the existing support at the front of the ledge is enough for drywall without additional framing.
reason: The reply gives a step-by-step method: level and straighten the top plate, add a 1x2 strip on the front edge, fill with rigid foam, set a metal angle on the back wall to a chalked level line, then hang the drywall. This deals with the uneven surface and the missing back support. Building a new flat plane with the strip, foam and back angle implicitly answers the framing question: build out a level support plane, though not full framing. Adding back support via the metal angle implies the front support alone is not enough. There is slight uncertainty because those last two answers are implied rather than stated outright.
label: Fully answered
